# TECHNICAL DECISIONS

Key decisions and their rationale. Grounded in the code; honest about what is
built vs roadmap.

---

## 1. Deterministic fixtures for the demo path
**Decision.** Core demo data is generated by a seeded PRNG (`utils.ts` mulberry32
+ `hashString`), so a query yields a byte-identical dataset every run
(`fixtures.ts`; test "is deterministic for a given query").
**Why.** Brief §31/§35: the demo must survive API failure, network loss, model
rate limits, and third-party changes. Determinism also makes the demo
*testable* and *reproducible* — the opposite of a flaky LLM live call.
**Honesty control.** The UI shows a persistent "Fixture dataset · deterministic"
pill and the Cloudinary status pill; fixtures are never presented as live data.

## 2. SSE for real event-driven progress (not a fake timer)
**Decision.** `engine.ts` builds an ordered event log (monotonic `seq`, ms `t`);
`/api/orchestra/run` streams it as Server-Sent Events; the client (`sse.ts`)
derives all progress from emitted events.
**Why.** Brief §5/§26 "do not fake progress." Using `fetch` + `ReadableStream`
(instead of `EventSource`) lets us pass a `speed` param and abort cleanly.
**Trade-off.** The event log is precomputed rather than emitted by long-running
agents; the *contract* (event shape, ordering) is production-real and the UI
cannot tell the difference.

## 3. Provenance-first data model
**Decision.** `Evidence` (sourceUrl, sourceType, sourceReliability, retrievedAt,
evidenceText, confidence) is attached per field; publishable records cannot carry
an un-cited non-name field (test-enforced). Conflicts retain *all* disagreeing
values + sources.
**Why.** Brief §6/§7: source-backed data is non-negotiable; disagreement must be
surfaced, not silently resolved. This is the primary anti-"LLM wrapper"
differentiator.

## 4. Explicit state machine over booleans
**Decision.** `WorkflowState` + `TRANSITIONS` + `canTransition` (`types.ts`);
illegal jumps rejected, happy path fully connected (both test-asserted).
**Why.** Brief §27. Workflows are recoverable (`FAILED → PLANNING` retry) and
auditable; no tangle of ad-hoc booleans.

## 5. Security posture (`src/lib/security.ts`) — implemented + tested
| Control | Function | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Prompt-injection scan (input) | `sanitizeQuery` → `{value, flagged}` | **Built**, wired into every route, tested |
| Injection scan (retrieved page text) | `scanRetrievedContent` | **Built + tested**; invoked on the (roadmap) live-retrieval path |
| SSRF guard | `isSafeUrl` (http(s) only; blocks localhost/private/link-local/metadata) | **Built + tested**; for live fetching |
| Upload allow-list | `isAllowedUpload` (jpeg/png/webp/mp4/mov) | **Built + tested**; for real uploads |
| Input length cap / control-char strip | `sanitizeQuery` (≤500 chars) | **Built + tested** |
**Why.** Brief §28: treat external content as untrusted *data*, never
instructions; server-side secrets; input validation.
**Honest gaps (roadmap):** **rate limiting**, **audit logs**, and signed uploads
are named in the brief but **not yet implemented**. `scanRetrievedContent` /
`isSafeUrl` / `isAllowedUpload` are unit-tested but only *exercised* once the
live web-research / real-upload paths exist; the deterministic demo exercises
`sanitizeQuery` in the routes.

## 6. Why Cloudinary is central (not a badge)
**Decision.** Cloudinary is the **media system of record**: `cloudinary.ts`
builds real transformation/delivery URLs when `CLOUDINARY_CLOUD_NAME` is set and
**preserves `originalAssetId` (public_id) through every transform** — the
provenance anchor. Structured metadata (typed/validated/searchable) is mapped via
`toStructuredMetadata`. With no cloud configured it falls back to a deterministic
placeholder so the product renders anyway.
**Why.** Brief §14: Cloudinary must be architecturally meaningful. Provenance +
transforms + structured metadata are load-bearing here, not decorative.
**Honest scope:** the demo uses placeholder delivery unless a cloud name is set;
signed uploads and live AI Video Analysis are roadmap (video "analysis" is
represented today by fixture `segments`).

## 7. Where Qdrant / Pathway / n8n fit — architectural, NOT wired
Per the brief's "no decorative sponsors" rule, these are honestly framed as the
production targets that the current deterministic seams stand in for. **None are
integrated in this repo** (no dependencies, no clients).

| Sponsor tech | Intended role | Current stand-in | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Qdrant** (Edge / hybrid dense+sparse) | IMPACTOS semantic retrieval index; low-latency local vector search with Edge↔Server sync | `search.ts` deterministic concept lexicon returning the same `SearchResult` (score + **reason**) shape | **Roadmap / not implemented** |
| **Pathway** (streaming ETL / real-time RAG) | Incremental ingestion of new field media + live re-indexing; ORCHESTRA incremental source updates | Batch fixture generation (`buildDataset`) + precomputed event log | **Roadmap / not implemented** |
| **n8n** (workflow orchestration) | Visual orchestration + triggers for the multi-agent runs; external tool execution | In-code plan/agent/event contracts (`plan.ts`, `engine.ts`, `AgentTrace`) | **Roadmap / not implemented** |

The design keeps these swap-in-able because each sits behind a typed contract
(`SearchResult`, `ResearchPlan`, `OrchestraEvent`/`AgentTrace`) that already
exists — adopting the real service does not change downstream code.

## 8. Framework & runtime choices
- **Next.js 15 App Router + API routes as backend** — one deployable, routes are
  thin wrappers over pure `src/lib` functions (easy to test, easy to swap for a
  service later). `runtime = "nodejs"` for streaming + Node APIs.
- **React 19 + Tailwind 3.4 + design tokens** — enterprise-console look with a
  small, typed component kit (`ui.tsx`); dark-only.
- **zod present** for schema validation at the boundary (dependency available;
  routes currently do lightweight manual validation).
- **Vitest** for fast unit tests over the deterministic core.

## 9. Known trade-offs / debt
- **Demo data is fixtures** — records + media are seeded and clearly labelled;
  the LLM and retrieval seams are deterministic stand-ins (see §1, §7). Full UI
  is built (`next build` passes with 23 routes).
- **No persistence / auth / multi-tenant** — stateless routes over fixtures.
- **Rate limiting & audit logs** not implemented (§5); live retrieval/upload
  guards built + tested but not yet invoked by a live path.
